distances = [dist(B, C), dist(A, C), dist(A, B)]
distances_sum = sum(distances)
distance_proportions = [distances_sum/dist for dist in distances]
distance_proportions_sum = sum(distance_proportions) 
probability_estimates = [dp/distance_proportions_sum for dp in distance_proportions]

## Normalized Probabilities From Embeddings
```{python}
from scipy.spatial.distance import cosine as cos_dist

def embeddings_to_probabilities(embeddings, contains_negatives, verbose=False):
    A, B, C = embeddings
    distances = [cos_dist(B, C), cos_dist(A, C), cos_dist(A, B)]
    if not contains_negatives:
        distances = [1-dist for dist in distances] # normalized distance assuming all-positive
    else:
        distances = [1-(dist+1)/2 for dist in distances] # normalized distance for possibly negative embeddings
    sum_distances = sum(distances)
    probability_estimates = [e/sum_distances for e in distances]

    if verbose:
        distances = [round(float(d), 3) for d in distances] # round for better readability
        probability_estimates = [round(float(p), 3) for p in probability_estimates] # round for better readability
        print()
        print(f"{'embeddings:':<16} {str(embeddings):>20}")
        print(f"{'distances:':<16} {str(distances):>20}")
        print(f"{'probabilities:':<16} {str(probability_estimates):>20}")
    return probability_estimates

A = [0, 0, 10]
B = [2, 0, 9]
C = [8, 6, 4]
embeddings_pos = [A, B, C]

D = [0, -1, 10]
E = [-2, 0, 9]
F = [-8, 6, 4]
embeddings_neg = [D, E, F]

probability_estimates = embeddings_to_probabilities(embeddings_pos, contains_negatives=False, verbose=True)
probability_estimates_neg = embeddings_to_probabilities(embeddings_neg, contains_negatives=True, verbose=True)

```

## Normalized Probabilities From Human Responses
```{python}

triplets_full = pd.read_parquet("data/triplets_full.parquet")
triplets = triplets_full[['image1','image2','image3']] - 1 #subtracting 1 so they're 0-indexed

# Identify unique unordered triplets
# eg. (12, 45, 87) and (87, 12, 45) are the same triplet.
df = triplets.copy()

sorted_ids = np.sort(
    df[["image1", "image2", "image3"]].to_numpy(),
    axis=1
)

group_cols = ["id_a", "id_b", "id_c"]

chosen_ids = triplets['image3']
df[group_cols] = sorted_ids
df["id_chosen"] = chosen_ids
df = df.drop(columns= ["image1", "image2", "image3"])

# Number of unique triplets
times_chosen = ["a_chosen", "b_chosen", "c_chosen"]


# Counts how many times each was chosen
agg = df.copy()
agg = (
    df.assign(**{
        count_col: agg[id_col].eq(agg["id_chosen"]).astype(int)
        for id_col, count_col in zip(group_cols, times_chosen)
    })
    .groupby(group_cols, as_index=False, sort=False)[times_chosen]
    .sum()
)

proportions = ["a_prop", "b_prop", "c_prop"]
agg[proportions] = agg[times_chosen].div(agg[times_chosen].sum(axis=1), axis=0)

agg_5plus = agg.loc[
    agg[["a_chosen", "b_chosen", "c_chosen"]].sum(axis=1) >= 5
].copy()
```

### Writing the aggregated variance to human_triplet_variance.csv
```{python}
agg_5plus.to_csv("data/agg_5plus.csv", index=False)
```
